thread:
Jules Ortega: heads up — customer AcmeCorp says their trial credits ended up on a legacy service account instead of their new project after an SSO reconnect. they need the credits moved asap.
Maya Chen: ugh. do we have org ids and creds? can you paste the workspace/org ids & a repro? :pray:
Jules Ortega: yes — reported ids: customer-visible org: acme-prod (org_01a9c3). credits landed on legacy service account: svc-acme-old (org_9d4f2a). User says they re-linked SSO yesterday.
Arun Patel: thanks. can you confirm whether this was an SSO account merge or a full restore? those behave differently in the sso-sync job.
Jules Ortega: support ticket notes: "SSO re-link (Okta) + restored previous directory mapping" — they did a restore from backup then re-linked. Support attached the sync logs.
Maya Chen: quick check — does the billing record show the credit grant tied to org_9d4f2a or to an account email? if it's org-scoped we need DB mapping fix; if it's email-scoped we can reassign.
Jules Ortega: billing shows grant id grant_7c3f attached to org_9d4f2a. support-bot uploaded logs (links): https://internal.acme/support/attach-log-789
support-bot: uploaded file: sso-sync-194321.log
Sophie Liao: looping in infra — @Sophie can you check if the sso-sync job created a duplicate mapping? my guess: after restore the old service account retained the original org_id and the grant reconciliation matched it.
Sophie Liao: I see a mismatch in the sync audit: user mapping re-created svc-acme-old with the same external_id as acme-prod. looks like the restore re-hydrated the service account row before the new org was registered.
Sophie Liao: repro steps I used locally:
```
# simulate restore + okta link
POST /admin/restore?backup=backup-2026-03-10
POST /sso/link {"external_id": "okta-acme", "org_id": "org_01a9c3"}
# reconciliation job then runs and attaches grants by external_id
```
Arun Patel: OK — so the grant reconciliation picks row by external_id then attaches any outstanding grants. if two rows share external_id the earlier (legacy) one wins.
Maya Chen: what's the safe remediation? can we move grant_7c3f to org_01a9c3 without breaking audit trails?
Sophie Liao: recommended path: (1) create a transfer audit event, (2) update grant.owner_org = org_01a9c3, (3) mark svc-acme-old as archived to prevent future matches. we should run a small migration script and record a reversible audit log.
Jules Ortega: customer requests ETA and manual fix today if possible. they have active tests failing.
Arun Patel: I'll prepare a DB patch and include an audit row. steps:
- lock grant row
- copy audit record with reason="manual_transfer: duplicate_sso_post_restore"
- update owner_org
- set svc-acme-old.status=archived
- re-run reconciliation dry-run to confirm no other grants will flip
Maya Chen: thanks. estimate 2-3 hours. please paste the PR/ops runbook here when ready. include rollback SQL.
Sophie Liao: putting a blocker on automatic reconciliation for that external_id until we've completed transfer (to avoid race). Arun — want ops permission to pause job for okta-acme now?
Arun Patel: authorized. pausing job and will run migration now. tagging the ticket: #SUP-4582
Jules Ortega: perfect. I'll update the customer: "we have a remediation plan, pausing background sync, and will transfer your credits within the next 3 hours. we'll follow up when complete." :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: post-mortem notes: consider making reconciliation prefer active orgs over archived rows or add a uniqueness constraint on external_id + active=true. filing a follow-up to eng-runtime.
support-bot: ticket SUP-4582 updated: operation in progress.
